name: Eleganz Interiors Limited
sector: Commercial interior fit-outs and design/build contracting
summary: Eleganz Interiors is a corporate fit-out and design/build contractor, not a proven high-quality compounder. Customer access and a sizeable order book support an execution-led growth/value thesis, but the decisive issue is converting work into unrestricted cash. FY26 revenue was ₹400.22 crore while net receivables reached ₹150.91 crore and operating cash flow was negative ₹13.34 crore. At the 19 October close of ₹86.90, trailing owner-earnings P/E is about 8.88x, which is not by itself cheap if collections or overseas obligations absorb capital. Business quality is 5.06/10 and growth quality is capped at 5.0 because cash conversion has been persistently weak. IAS is NS: conditional domestic/core valuation is useful, but unverified Singapore acquisition economics prevent a supported whole-group entry conclusion. Verified collections, a current bank/claims bridge and disclosed acquisition cost would change this assessment. [S1][S11][S14]
identity_note: Issuer annual report, prospectus and NSE SM metadata agree on ISIN, shares and listing identity. [S1][S3][S14]
score_note: BQS and GQS scored with complete historical-factor coverage; GQS cash-conversion cap applies. R/P/IAS NS for the unverified current acquisition/claims perimeter. Core return diagnostics are not a whole-group fair value.

gates.reason: No substantiated severe promoter diversion or repeated minority-abuse finding established. The disclosed allegation is against employees/suppliers and describes fraud on the company, not by promoters. Controls and acquisition disclosure require follow-through.

Unmodified statements and reconciled cash-equivalent classification support historical P&L/cash use with Medium overall confidence. The standalone bank-return disagreement is unresolved and Annexure 1 was not located; do not infer a quantified misstatement or accept unverified drawing-power headroom. Current acquisition perimeter is inadequate for whole-group IAS.

Restrained survival without new bank credit or warrant conversion remains funded, including a 15-day temporary collection-lag test with about ₹0.75 crore minimum cash. Growth-case timing and debt-call variants fail without additional liquidity; exact current rights/claim dates are unverified. No actual default asserted and no arbitrary stacked-stress Fail applied.

Eligible SM series and observed trades, but 1,000-share lot and constrained turnover make execution material. Illustrative ₹5 lakh exit takes 5.92 sessions at 5% of conservative 60-day turnover, not a guaranteed fill.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Eleganz Interiors is a corporate fit-out and design/build contractor, not a proven high-quality compounder. Customer access and a sizeable order book support an execution-led growth/value thesis, but the decisive issue is converting work into unrestricted cash. FY26 revenue was ₹400.22 crore while net receivables reached ₹150.91 crore and operating cash flow was negative ₹13.34 crore. At the 19 October close of ₹86.90, trailing owner-earnings P/E is about 8.88x, which is not by itself cheap if collections or overseas obligations absorb capital. Business quality is 5.06/10 and growth quality is capped at 5.0 because cash conversion has been persistently weak. IAS is NS: conditional domestic/core valuation is useful, but unverified Singapore acquisition economics prevent a supported whole-group entry conclusion. Verified collections, a current bank/claims bridge and disclosed acquisition cost would change this assessment. [S1][S11][S14]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Eleganz Interiors Limited, NSE SME ELGNZ, ISIN INE0R9101015; incorporated 18 April 1996, with operating roots described as 1988. Listing date is 14 February 2025. Cutoff is 20 October 2026; the last market session was 19 October. Actual issued equity is 22,599,626 shares, market capitalization ₹196.39 crore. Up to 800,000 warrants could increase shares to 23,399,626, but outstanding warrants are not already-issued equity. Research uses Indian-GAAP consolidated accounts, distinguishing the parent-only auditor comments and equity-accounted associates. Five-year rolling scenario horizon, 15% nominal pre-tax equity hurdle; 12% and 18% sensitivities; ₹5 lakh is an illustrative liquidity reference, not a proposed allocation.

G1 is Conditional, not a severe integrity Fail; G2 is Conditional because historical audited accounts remain usable but bank-return reconciliation and current perimeter need follow-through; G3 is Conditional, with both surviving and failed funding sensitivities; G4 is Conditional, tradable but thin. High confidence applies to inspected reported P&L, balance figures and dated exchange turnover. Medium applies to economic comparability, working-capital recoverability, moat and governance judgments. Current acquisition/funding perimeter has Low confidence, making IAS NS without erasing otherwise supported historical factors. Forecast uncertainty is not the same as uncertainty about an audited historical number. [S1][S3][S8][S11][S14][S15]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS = 0.20×4 + 0.20×5 + 0.12×8 + 0.10×6 + 0.12×5 + 0.10×3 + 0.08×5 + 0.08×5 = 5.06, displayed 5.1. GQS = 0.40×8 + 0.20×6 + 0.15×5 + 0.15×5 + 0.10×3 = 6.20; persistent CASH=3 caps the final at 5.0. Both have full factor coverage and Medium weakest material factor confidence. This cap does not claim CAP itself has demonstrated persistent value destruction.

Canonical factors: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 5. No historical 9–10 is awarded. IAS reuses Q=5.06 exactly, D=4 and L=4; R and P are NS. Its scored weight is 55%, not reweighted to 100%; raw aggregate is NS and missing-factor arithmetic bounds are 2.915–6.965, not a target range or recommendation. There is no governance or funding cap asserted, and no averaging of BQS and GQS. Factor audit supplies at least two evidence links and contrary evidence for each numeric judgment. BQS/GQS may be compared provisionally with similarly qualified research; IAS cannot rank. [S1][S3][S11][S14]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
The company combines design-and-build with general contracting for commercial interiors. It executes civil/interior work, mechanical/electrical/plumbing systems, furniture and associated fit-out scopes for offices, research facilities, laboratories and airports. Money is earned through project execution and certification rather than recurring subscriptions. A project can be physically advanced before final certification, retention release or customer cash arrives, while vendors and statutory claims still need funding.

The operating base is predominantly India. FY26 service revenue to the Singapore associate was about ₹2.06 crore; the associate is not equivalent to consolidated foreign operating revenue. The existing roughly 27,000-square-foot factory and subcontracting network offer delivery capacity, but outsourced inputs and labour mean headline revenue is not a measure of proprietary product units. FY26 revenue less cost of goods and inventory change was about ₹113.36 crore, a value-added proxy, not a separately reported net-revenue segment. There is no verified product-volume/price bridge, so none is invented. [S1][S3][S6]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is qualification, coordinated project execution and client relationships: buyers need timely handover across several technical disciplines, and proven vendors can win repeat assignments. It is not established pricing power or a protected network. FY24 top-five clients contributed 63.36% and top ten 78.04%; orders were nonexclusive and not assured by long-term purchase commitments. Latest concentration remains a gap. A delayed or lost large project can therefore affect both billing and cash.

Three relevant operating comparators are Ambience Interiors, Space Matrix Design Consultants and Cherry Hill. ICRA reports Ambience FY25 operating income ₹600.9 crore and 9.7% OPBDITA margin; CARE reports Space Matrix ₹846.90 crore and 6.63% PBIDT margin. Their different scopes and dates show that project execution can operate at scale with mid/high-single-digit margins, not that Eleganz deserves a peer-average multiple. Cherry Hill describes overlapping turnkey, civil, MEP and fit-out services; its promotional experience/repeat-client claims are not independent financial evidence. The prospectus itself did not identify a comparable listed pure play. Competition, concentration and low exclusivity support MOAT 5, while real qualifications and order access are the contrary evidence against treating the business as wholly undifferentiated. [S3][S16][S17][S18]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Reported revenue, ₹crore: FY21 144.85; FY22 153.83; FY23 190.26; FY24 221.29; FY25 392.71; FY26 400.22. Annual additions were ₹8.98, ₹36.43, ₹31.03, ₹171.41 and ₹7.52 crore. The chosen scoring window is FY23–FY26: 28.13% CAGR. The available FY21–FY26 CAGR is 22.54%, but the starting year suffered the pandemic and a ₹13.66 crore owner loss, so it is not a clean normal-cycle organic base. Both calculations fall in the 20–30% revenue band; no additional small-base penalty or convenient period switching is used.

FY25 growth of 77.46% was followed by only 1.91% in FY26. July's provisional Q1 FY27 update reports ₹74.26 crore versus ₹52.90 crore, +40.37%, but one quarter is neither annualized nor used for a REV upgrade. The core domestic revenue base is broadly comparable; overseas equity-accounted sales are not added as group revenue. Project mix, purchased material pass-through and certification timing prevent a verified physical-volume/price split. The selected score is 8 with Medium economic-comparability confidence, rather than an unsupported 9 or 10. [S1][S3][S4][S7]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The March order book was reported at ₹546 crore; June quarter intake ₹148.96 crore and June backlog ₹621.46 crore suggest ongoing access to demand. Simple opening backlog plus intake less quarterly revenue gives ₹620.70 crore, about ₹0.76 crore below the reported closing number. Scope, revisions or rounding may explain it, but there is no complete reconciliation. The roughly ₹2,600 crore bid pipeline is not firm backlog. The August IT-client revision is a revised total, not an additional full ₹129.11 crore order to count twice. September/October smaller awards do not solve the cash question.

A bottom-up scaling path needs projects won, executed, certified and paid, supported by subcontractors, bank guarantees and retention funding. Management's 25% growth and 9–10% EBITDA aspirations are not the base case. The core base uses 10%, 10%, 10%, 8%, 8% revenue growth, operating EBITDA after financing commissions moving from 8.2% to 8.7%, and operating capital improving from 31.97% of revenue to 29%. Cash capex is ₹7/8/5/5/5 crore, an analyst allowance rather than a verified factory budget. A factory plan described as a roughly two-year project has no adequately established full cost/return schedule. The bull needs faster conversion, lower operating-capital intensity and higher margins, not just a larger TAM.

FY26 conventional all-capital after-tax return proxy, before treating borrowing/BG commissions as operating costs, is about 12.0%; the FY24–FY26 incremental proxy is 7.9%. A 12–15% analytical capital-cost range makes these mixed, not clear durable excess-return evidence. IPO-funded assets may be immature, so CAP=5 rather than declaring every rupee wasted. GQS nevertheless falls from 6.2 raw to 5.0 because three profitable years produced negative aggregate CFO. [S1][S6][S7][S19][S20][S21]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter ownership is about 69.23%; the reviewed June declaration reports no encumbrance for the stated period, not a guarantee about every future date. Related-party remuneration/fees include ₹3.25 crore for Sameer Pakvasa, ₹0.6313 crore for Mayank Sharma and ₹1.5762 crore founder fees to Akshay Pakvasa. These are disclosed transactions requiring proportionality scrutiny, not automatic abuse. A ₹0.50 crore director borrowing was repaid, with no ending amount from that item. Warrant terms are ₹83 per share equivalent with 25% upfront; receipt and dilution are separately modeled.

Promises versus delivery: the earlier FY26 revenue expectation of about ₹430 crore was revised and actual revenue was ₹400.22 crore; management did not characterize the whole miss as April spillover. The May expectation of about ₹130 crore collections in three months has not been verified with a subsequent cash-flow statement. June-quarter provisional revenue improves, but does not certify collections. The factory timetable lacks a fully budgeted return case. January approval proposed buying the remaining Singapore stake; May management comments describe the partner leaving, yet a verified consideration/completion/assumed-claims bridge is absent. The small SAR Universal approval, 10,000 shares at ₹10, is a ₹0.01 crore proposal and not an independent reason to suppress all historical scores.

The FY2026 annual report describes an alleged fraud on the company involving present/former employees and suppliers, with a tentative ₹99.71 lakh amount in the FIR. The investigation was ongoing and the final amount and financial impact were not ascertainable. This is not a finding of promoter fraud or established diversion by management. The board describes reporting under section 143(12), while the parent CARO report states that no ADT-4 had been filed; these disclosures are not treated as a resolved legal characterization. [S1]

The parent auditor reports that quarterly statements submitted to banks did not agree with the books and refers to Annexure 1. The quantitative annexure was not located in the reviewed report, so neither the size nor the cause of the differences is established. The group CARO summary and parent detail are not silently treated as identical. The audit opinion and internal-financial-control opinion are unmodified, and the auditor reports no lender default or wilful-defaulter status. No quantified asset overstatement or actual funding default is inferred. [S1]

The annual report records a structured digital database/UPSI-entry delay through 30 June 2025; the company says the software was installed from 1 July 2025 and entries were maintained thereafter. This is a disclosed process lapse and company response, not evidence of insider trading. [S1]

These distinct issues support GOV 4 and EXEC 5, without invoking the severe-governance override or converting personnel changes into statutory-auditor resignation. [S1][S6][S8][S11][S12][S22]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Owner PAT, ₹crore, FY21 through FY26: −13.66, 5.09, 10.31, 12.21, 20.71, 22.11. CFO: 13.32, −5.78, 1.35, −3.65, 2.54, −13.34. Cash capex: 0.17, 0.25, 2.88, 2.35, 4.33, 12.01. FY21 cash release during a loss year is not durable conversion; FY22–FY24 use prospectus restated figures rather than mixing original tax restatements into the trend. FY24–FY26 CFO/PAT is −26.25%, and capex-subtracted FCF totals −₹33.12 crore.

FY26 revenue ₹400.2231 crore less goods/WIP costs ₹286.8597 crore leaves ₹113.3634 crore before employees and other operating costs. Normalized operating EBITDA before borrowing/BG commissions is about ₹34.3474 crore; treating ₹1.4119 crore of non-interest borrowing/BG charges as operating cost gives a model starting EBITDA about ₹32.9355 crore. Other income includes ₹4.4504 crore deposit interest. The ₹0.5974 crore exceptional gratuity charge and ₹0.8595 crore associate loss are separated, not rolled into recurring operating margins. Owner earnings, rather than standalone promotional PAT, underpin the 8.88x trailing P/E. Reported EPS is ₹9.78 versus ₹9.16; actual issued shares, not a presumed weighted share count, determine current valuation.

The cash-flow bridge reports pre-WC cash ₹38.6933 crore, WC absorption ₹44.0388 crore and taxes ₹7.9901 crore, resulting in CFO −₹13.3356 crore. Inventory released ₹32.6077 crore while receivables absorbed ₹108.2440 crore; supplier/other liability increases partly financed the gap. Net AR rose from ₹43.2547 crore to ₹150.9054 crore. Gross AR over one year is about ₹8.1707 crore; retention receivables of ₹30.5374 crore are separate balance assets, not added again via AS-7 contract disclosures.

FY25 CFO appears as ₹4.0251 crore in the original report and ₹2.5413 crore in the FY26 comparative. The approximately ₹1.4838 crore difference tracks cash-equivalent/fixed-deposit and other-asset classification, while balance-sheet cash is unchanged at ₹10.1880 crore. The ₹0.4513 crore prior-tax presentation shift cancels across the bridge. This is not characterized as missing cash.

Opening cash for operations is only ₹12.9140 crore under the disclosed-lien assumption. ₹49.70 crore OD-pledged deposits and ₹9.2753 crore BG margin are not freely available working capital. Reported gross debt is ₹41.9116 crore including accrued interest; model principal sums differ by ₹0.0001 crore because of note rounding. Net debt excluding restricted deposits is about ₹28.99 crore. Current statutory liabilities ₹12.6926 crore, provisions ₹0.6355 crore and lease-equalisation ₹0.0804 crore are paid explicitly; current term ₹0.3003 crore and accrued interest ₹0.0069 crore are not hidden in WC. Noncurrent employee claims plus ₹0.0889 crore unrecognized gratuity are partly paid and the residue deducted at exit. Future benefit expense is funded in operating costs and does not erase legacy obligations. Statutory assets ₹7.9021 crore receive zero core recovery, avoiding double-counted tax credits; a separate recovery variant adds them once.

Operating capital ₹127.9560 crore consistently includes receivables, WIP, retentions, other operating advances/security and deducts trade, customer/mobilization/retention/expense liabilities. The claim map contains every reported opening category. Conventional EBIT-based ROCE of 16.66%, after-tax proxy 12.00%, and incremental proxy 7.90% retain IPO/cash capital in the denominator and are not project IRRs. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹86.90 the market value is ₹196.39 crore. A simple P/E of 8.88x and a gross-debt/free-cash enterprise value around ₹225.38 crore imply about 6.84x the ₹32.94 crore core operating EBITDA proxy, before separately valuing pledged deposits and legacy claims. Treating all ₹49.70 crore OD deposits as available today would materially overstate operating liquidity. The primary valuation is a cash/debt-linked core operating EBITDA exit, not a peer-average P/E.

Bear core, no rescue: year-5 revenue ₹401.28 crore, EBITDA ₹30.10 crore, exit 5x EBITDA, cash ₹77.48 crore, debt ₹41.04 crore, terminal price ₹104.53, funded five-year return 3.76%.

Base core, no new bank line: year-5 revenue ₹621.34 crore, EBITDA ₹54.06 crore, exit 7x EBITDA, cash ₹85.03 crore, debt ₹41.04 crore, terminal price ₹201.59, funded five-year return 18.33%.

Bull core, no new bank line: year-5 revenue ₹802.92 crore, EBITDA ₹80.29 crore, exit 9x EBITDA, cash ₹94.15 crore, debt ₹41.04 crore, terminal price ₹352.60, funded five-year return 32.33%.

Bear assumptions are −10%, 0%, 3%, 4%, 4% revenue growth; 6.5% to 7.5% margins; opening operating-capital ratio retained plus initially 15 collection days; ₹3 crore annual maintenance capex; no warrant conversion. Base assumptions are stated in section 7. Bull uses 20%, 18%, 15%, 12%, 10% growth, 9% to 10% margins, capital intensity improving to 27%, and ₹12/12/7/7/7 crore capex. These are analyst scenarios, not forecasts endorsed by the issuer. All three pay modeled legacy claims, cash tax, interest and compulsory term amortization; no new bank line or unreceived IPO cash is assumed.

Terminal equity adds free cash, conditional OD-deposit recovery and ₹1.1047 crore property/society value to operating EV, subtracting debt and remaining employee claims. BG margin remains required operating capital, associates have zero assumed upside, and unspent dedicated warrants are not free excess cash. No dividends are assumed. Warrant conversion adds ₹4.98 crore only at month 12 and 800,000 shares; a no-conversion variant is separately funded. Borrowing and deposit interest are separately taxed, not included in the exit EBITDA multiple.

Core base terminal value supports diagnostic entry prices of ₹114.39, ₹100.23 and ₹88.12 at 12%, 15% and 18% hurdles. These are not a whole-group buy range. Excluding terminal OD-deposit recovery lowers core base IRR to 15.72%. At 7x terminal EBITDA, roughly 4.20% constant revenue growth meets a 15% hurdle under the other model assumptions; at 5x it requires roughly 14.46%, demonstrating multiple dependence. A complete growth×multiple grid and 12/15/18% reverse tests are supplied. No probability-weighted average of scenario returns is called an IRR.

The crucial unresolved variable is current Singapore cash cost and assumed obligations. A zero-to-₹20 crore purchase/funding sensitivity plus ₹1.7134 crore annual losses is explicitly hypothetical, not an estimate of consideration. ₹5 crore cost leaves only about ₹0.63 crore minimum core cash; ₹10 crore produces an unfunded ₹4.37 crore gap. Because this unknown can cross the funding boundary, assigning a supported whole-group R or P would be false precision. IAS remains NS despite the attractive-looking core base arithmetic. [S1][S8][S11][S14]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is that reported growth is a receivable-financed project cycle rather than cash-generating compounding. Concentrated clients can delay certifications, retention recovery can lag, and banks may restrict drawing power precisely when suppliers, taxes and employee claims mature. A low trailing P/E then capitalizes earnings the shareholder cannot distribute. Overseas support or a factory overrun can consume the remaining buffer.

The ordinary bear is funded but earns only 3.76%, well below the 15% hurdle. A base-growth scenario with a temporary 15-day collection delay reaches a ₹7.69 crore cash shortfall even though its eventual year-end receipts recover; shareholder IRR is deliberately null. A hypothetical ₹25 crore line funds that path with about ₹7.76 crore drawn, including draw-related interest. That hypothetical line is not evidence that the issuer can borrow it. Removing discretionary expansion and warrant conversion gives a restrained survival countercase: with −10% initial sales, 7.5% margin and maintenance capex, even a temporary 15-day lag retains about ₹0.75 crore minimum cash. This prevents equating optional-growth financing with an automatic survival Fail.

Calling the demand revolver without simultaneous deposit setoff creates about ₹30.79 crore shortfall; allowing contemporaneous pledged-deposit setoff leaves the countercase funded. Legal rights and current lender terms are unverified. A 40-day extra-collection/6.5%-margin boundary fails by about ₹10.86 crore, but is labeled severe and is not stacked with every tax, fraud and BG loss to manufacture G3 Fail. A separate ₹8.1707 crore receivable loss reduces recoverable opening assets, adds back the noncash charge once, and funds replacement capital once. Full identified non-bank contingent settlement also crosses a thin buffer, but simultaneous settlement is a sensitivity, not the base.

The FY2026 notes disclose disputed service-tax principal and penalty of ₹1.7556 crore each, income-tax ₹0.3154 crore, GST ₹0.1863 crore and ₹0.0634 crore, and ₹0.2322 crore TRACES demand under reconciliation. They also describe a ₹1.1537 crore POSCO commercial matter in mediation and a ₹1.9805 crore Aren Matrix unbooked-bill claim before the MSME mechanism. These are disclosed disputed/reconciled claims, not established wrongdoing or assumed simultaneous cash losses. Their current outcomes were not located. Bank guarantees and letters of credit account for most of the ₹133.6203 crore total contingent disclosure and are not all expected losses. [S1]

Thesis-break variables are verified overdue/retention deterioration despite stated collections, unavailable renewal/setoff, or acquisition/support commitments that exceed funded liquidity. These model outcomes are conditional on assumed timing and stale opening balances; no actual default is alleged. [S1][S3][S6][S11][S13]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold price in five years requires 37.97% annual appreciation; tenfold requires 58.49%. Using fully converted existing warrants, a 10% operating EBITDA margin and 7x exit multiple, an optimistic zero-net-debt benchmark requires about ₹1,452 crore revenue for 5× and ₹2,905 crore for 10×. Those imply 29.4% and 48.7% revenue CAGRs from FY26. At 9x, the corresponding revenues are about ₹1,130 crore and ₹2,259 crore, still requiring 23.1% and 41.4% growth.

These are feasibility hurdles, not forecasts or evidence that the funding exists. They assume a stronger margin than the current normalized base, no extra dilution beyond known warrants and no adverse net-debt claim. Existing backlog does not establish five years of replenishment at those scales. The current core bull produces about 4.06× terminal price, below 5×, while timing/funding gaps already appear at much smaller scale. A 10× thesis is unsupported without substantially improved collections, capital productivity and independently funded demand. [S1][S7][S8][S14]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: The monitoring table tracks nine company-specific tests: collections, ageing/retentions, bank/FD rights, Singapore perimeter, backlog conversion, margin/capital returns, warrant/factory cash, control/legal follow-through and executable liquidity. Baselines and warning/thesis-break thresholds are explicit below. Review on the next relevant filed half-year/annual result, bank or acquisition disclosure, not an assumed automatic monitoring service. Price alone can change IAS arithmetic but cannot repair cash conversion or upgrade BQS/GQS. [S1][S6][S7][S8][S11][S14]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Mixed-quality project contractor; cash-conversion and execution-dependent growth/value thesis. BQS 5.1 and GQS 5.0 do not satisfy high-quality compounder criteria. IAS is unscoreable rather than classified attractive from a core-only return; no favorable whole-group investment classification or numerical IAS ranking is issued. G1 is not failed, G3 is not automatically failed from optional-growth or extreme-stress models, and G4 is not labeled suspended.

Conditional action category: research watchlist pending current funding/perimeter evidence. Lower prices improve core expected return, but do not answer whether acquisition/legacy commitments can be funded. A defensible entry assessment requires actual Singapore consideration/claims, current bank terms and credible collected cash. Conversely, verified collection normalization with stable margins and disciplined investment would support reconsideration. This is analytical research, not a trade, portfolio allocation or promised return. [S1][S11][S14]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary annual reports, signed historical accounts, the NSE prospectus, exchange capital/operating filings and official trading data anchor the analysis. Management guidance and provisional updates remain attributed statements. Rating reports contextualize economics and old facilities; the October 2025 Acuite action was an upgrade followed by withdrawal with lender NOC, not a current sanctioned-cash balance or a noncooperation finding. Relevant competitor sources are used only within their actual scope.

All tables are converted to ₹crore consistently from ₹lakh or original rupees. Five-year projections are analyst assumptions with linked operating capital, capex, tax, interest, dedicated proceeds, term amortization and terminal claims. They start from a conditional March-to-October balance proxy, not fabricated interim accounts. No unsupported recovery is assigned to statutory assets or associates; no double-counting of AS-7 contract subtotals, IPO cash, pledged deposits, accrued interest or current benefit provisions is allowed.

Open questions are specific: current Singapore purchase/support obligations; current bank drawing power and deposit rights; quantified bank Annexure 1; exact statutory-credit components and legacy payment timing; latest concentration and order-book revisions; verified post-March collections; final legal/investigation outcomes; live trading depth. These gaps determine which conclusions are conditional and why IAS, rather than every historical factor, is NS. Exact source URLs, dates, locators and evidence types are in the source ledger and audit. [S1][S2][S3][S6][S8][S11][S13][S14]

limitations: March 2026 audited balances are a conditional October opening proxy, not verified current cash, debt or working capital. June warrant receipt is included only as a dedicated-use proxy; intervening deployment is unavailable.

Singapore purchase price, completed ownership, assumed liabilities and any support commitments are not verified. The model gives core and explicit funding sensitivities, not whole-group fair value; R, P and IAS remain NS.
Current bank sanctions, drawing power, debt-renewal terms and legal deposit-release/setoff rights are not verified. Old rated facilities are not current available cash.

The bank-return disagreement lacks a located quantitative Annexure 1. Statutory-asset tax composition and exact legacy settlement dates are not separately disclosed; conservative payments/recoveries are assumptions, not issuer due-date findings.
Latest customer concentration, organic/acquired and price/volume split, and a full order-book reconciliation are unavailable. A single provisional quarter cannot validate growth or cash conversion.
The employee/supplier matter and identified legal/tax disputes remain unresolved in the reviewed sources; no later closure located. No allegation is generalized to promoter fraud or actual default.
Live market depth, spread and future circuit exit capacity were not observed. Historical liquidity and caution flags do not guarantee trading access.
next_steps: Reconcile current Singapore consideration, assumed liabilities and funding.
Obtain current bank/FD rights and bank-return reconciliation.
Verify collection and half-year cash evidence before converting core diagnostics into IAS.

GOV.reason: Unresolved bank-return reconciliation and documented control weaknesses constrain stewardship; acquisition economics are insufficiently specified. These are specific disclosure/control concerns, not substantiated promoter diversion.
GOV.contrary_evidence: Unmodified audit/IFC, no reported lender default, explicit upfront warrant receipt and no disclosed promoter pledge. No G1 severe-failure override.

MOAT.reason: Qualified execution, design-plus-build delivery and repeat corporate access are useful but contestable; concentrated, nonexclusive projects and several larger competitors prevent a structural-moat conclusion.
MOAT.contrary_evidence: Long operating history and ₹621.46 crore reported backlog indicate real customer access, not an undifferentiated startup.

REV.reason: Chosen before scoring: FY23–FY26 three-year reported core-revenue CAGR 28.13%, band 8. Five-year endpoint is COVID distorted. No trajectory adjustment from a single strong quarter; no extra small-base deduction.
REV.contrary_evidence: FY26 grew only 1.91% after a 77.46% prior-year expansion. Price, mix and unit volumes are not separately available; no proven five-year organic CAGR, score ceiling 8.

DUR.reason: Office/R&D/airport fit-out access and backlog support several years of opportunity; Q1 intake corroborates demand. Funding, concentration and discretionary tenant capex limit dependable duration.
DUR.contrary_evidence: ₹2,600 crore bid pipeline and 25% management growth target are not firm realizable revenue. Factory economics and revised order timing are not fully budgeted.

CAP.reason: All-capital after-tax return proxy about 12% is around the lower part of an assumed 12–15% capital-cost range; FY24–26 incremental proxy 7.90% is weak but includes immature IPO-funded deployment. Score reflects mixed cohorts, not proven durable value destruction.
CAP.contrary_evidence: An asset-light project model and backlog provide a route to improve utilization. Capital returns would improve only if collections and capital productivity actually normalize.

CASH.reason: Profitable FY24–26 cumulative CFO is negative, with ₹33.12 crore negative FCF and a ₹107.65 crore receivable increase in FY26. This is persistent poor cash realization, not only a single capex year.
CASH.contrary_evidence: Inventory released ₹32.61 crore in FY26; part of March billing may collect later. No proof of ₹130 crore forecast collections yet. Classification change is not treated as missing cash.

BAL.reason: Existing claims are manageable in a restrained survival countercase but cash is timing-sensitive and debt is callable/secured. Restricted deposits cannot fund routine operations without lender consent.
BAL.contrary_evidence: Large pledged FD can support a legally permitted simultaneous debt setoff; auditor reports no lender default. No hypothetical new line is used to declare survival.

EXEC.reason: Substantial FY25 scaling and continuing orders coexist with the missed FY26 target, collection slippage and unclear overseas integration economics. Mixed rather than consistently strong delivery.
EXEC.contrary_evidence: Management revised the missed projection instead of asserting it all shifted into April; provisional Q1 revenue improves, but is not proof of cash or full-year delivery.

EARN.reason: Owner PAT grew about 6.76%, but deposit interest and associate losses materially affect the bridge. Current-share EPS ₹9.78 versus ₹9.16 progresses only modestly.
EARN.contrary_evidence: Core operating profit remains positive; the ₹0.5974 crore gratuity charge depresses current earnings rather than inflating them. No fabricated normalized EPS growth from bonus/IPO denominators.

R.reason: A conditional core return is calculable, but a supported current whole-group base return cannot be asserted without acquisition price, claims and current funding. IAS R remains NS.
R.contrary_evidence: Core sensitivity is informative: 18.33% at the selected ordinary assumptions, not a substitute for the missing perimeter.

D.reason: Credible timing stress can demand new funding; all-claim/payment and financing-call boundaries are material, even when a restrained no-growth case survives. Thin cash headroom supports a lower resilience band.
D.contrary_evidence: The restrained temporary-delay case survives without rescue and the ordinary bear earns a modest positive terminal return. No demonstrated actual insolvency or automatic G3 Fail.

P.reason: Core reverse expectations are computable, but a whole-group price-implied expectation score would conceal an unverified cash/claim perimeter.
P.contrary_evidence: At 7x core operating EBITDA the model can reach the hurdle with about 4.20% growth, but this assumes the specified collection, margin and terminal bridge.

L.reason: 60-day conservative turnover yields 5.92 days and starting score 5. One combined implementation downgrade to 4 reflects the ₹86,900 lot, thin latest trades, concentration/irregular-trading flags and weaker recent turnover.
L.contrary_evidence: All 60 sessions show trades, SM is eligible, and status 6 means price discovery, not suspension. Missing live spread alone does not force NS.
